page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 236 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, as reflected in the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. However, memory bandwidth is a notable tradeoff, with both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth testing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang show weaker performance profiles.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and bundled local NVMe SSD, the D4ads_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads that require fast local scratch space but do not demand extreme memory bandwidth. It is well-suited for static web serving, text processing, and lightweight Redis deployments, where it achieves average throughput. It is less suitable for memory-bound database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference due to documented performance bottlenecks in those areas.
